Code derivation: data/yao_2020_intolerance_uncertainty.py melts the source columns matching 'ius\d+' by name, so the IRW code IS the source column name (no positional step); what is inferred is that column ius{i} is IUS item i in the canonical 27-item numbering. Tested in verify_yao_2020_ius.R (1402 live respondents aligned to .sav rows, 0 cell mismatches; 1402 responses on every item): P1 ius24 'keeps me from sleeping soundly' is the strongest of 27 IUS correlates of BDI item 16 (sleep in both BDI-I and BDI-II): 0.306 vs next 0.207 (ius26); P2 the published two-factor key (F1 = 1,2,3,9,12,13,14,15,16,17,20,22,23,24,25; F2 = rest) gives within-minus-between r 0.0428 against a 99th percentile of 0.0272 over 10,000 random 15/12 partitions (p = 0.0004); P3 the five items with the lowest mean inter-item r (ius10 0.076, ius21 0.166, ius19 0.170, ius4 0.217, ius18 0.229) are all Factor 2 items (chance ~0.01); P4 every item correlates positively with the GAD-7 total (0.046 for ius10 to 0.402), so resp is stored raw with 5 = most characteristic. Disclosed misses: the reciprocal of P1 does not hold (ius24's top BAI/BDI/GAD correlate is gad3 0.328, then gad4 0.318, then bdi16 0.306), and the IUS-12 prospective/inhibitory split does not beat random partitions of those 12 items (p = 0.46; the prospective items 10/19/21 correlate weakly with everything).
